blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY — An alleged ban on wearing a hijab, a traditional headscarf worn by Muslim women, by a college here has stirred controversy in Northern Mindanao (Region 10), prompting the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) to bring a complaint against the school before the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). Ustadz Abdul Jabbar Montañer, director of Al-Jalis As-Salih Inc., said they received complaints against Iligan Medical Center College’s (IMCC) alleged policy against wearing hijab during certain school activities. But in a statement on Saturday, the IMCC denied prohibiting Muslim students from wearing hijabs on campus. READ: Marcos signs law honoring […]...
